title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not part of the 1976 notes on the divided-power de Rham complex. It is a typed page, numbered 'IX – 31', from Grothendieck's SGA 7 Exposé IX, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie'. It is upside down relative to the manuscript, so the sheet was evidently reused as scrap paper for the notes. The adjacent manuscript pages compute endomorphisms of the semi-simplicial divided-power differential algebra A_* in connection with cohomology operations. They have no mathematical link to this page.

Content of the page, in modern terms. S is a Dedekind (or regular one-dimensional) base with function field K, and A is the Néron model of an abelian variety A_K.

3.3.2. The equivalent conditions of 3.2 give a partial stability of Néron models under base change. These conditions say that the identity component A^0 has semi-abelian fibres (an extension of an abelian variety by a torus). Equivalently, A_K extends to a smooth separated commutative group scheme over S with connected semi-abelian fibres.
- What is stable: for S'→S as in 3.3, with Néron model A' of A_{K'}, the map A^0 ×_S S' → A'^0 is an isomorphism.
- What is not stable: unless A_K has good reduction, the full map A ×_S S' → A' need not be an isomorphism. This holds even for S' finite over S and K'/K separable. The failure is precisely on the groups of connected components of the fibres; 11.10 later describes how these groups change.

Definition 3.4. A_K has semi-stable reduction over S if the equivalent conditions (i) and (ii) of 3.2 hold. The terminology is credited to Mumford, with a remark that it harmonises with the notions of stability in his book [17] (Geometric Invariant Theory).

3.4.0. Two remarks on the definition.
- Form (ii) does not mention Néron models at all.
- The condition is local on S, so one reduces to S a trait (by 3.2.1). Since forming the Néron model commutes with passing to the henselisation or strict henselisation, one may even assume S is a strictly local trait.

This is the standard setup leading to Grothendieck's semi-stable reduction theorem.
errors: No mathematical errors. There is a small typographical slip in the typescript: 'au cas S où S est un trait strictement local' has a redundant 'S'.

ideas.what: Stability of the identity component of the Néron model under base change in the semi-stable case; the component groups are not stable.
ideas.modern_name: Base-change behaviour of Néron models under semi-stable reduction

ideas.what: Definition of semi-stable reduction of an abelian variety via semi-abelian identity components or extensions; terminology attributed to Mumford.
Reduction of the semi-stability condition to a strictly henselian trait, using compatibility of Néron models with henselisation.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a page of the published SGA 7 Exposé IX typescript, reused upside down as scrap paper. Its content is fully published and well known.
transcription_corrections: The page is upside down relative to the surrounding manuscript; it is a typed page of SGA 7 Exposé IX (header 'IX', page '- 31 -').
The stamp reads 349; '343' appears crossed out; '182' is the handwritten archive page number.
